items.title: Analyserte krimbøker: – Romanen du skriver med KI, er ikke den samme som du hadde skrevet uten KI
items.excerpt: Aftenposten ran a stylometric analysis of Norwegian crime bestseller Jørn Lier Horst's novels before and after he began using AI: humming, 'during' and over a hundred times as many dashes — the language measurably shifted. Centre of Norway's biggest AI-authorship row.
items.rationale: Data-driven look at how AI use measurably changes a bestselling author's prose; it is the main piece on Norway's Horst affair and has not run before (the NRK follow-up on the same affair was dropped).

items.title: Risikerer vi at teknologien blir portvokter for litteraturen?
items.excerpt: Norway's writers' union Forfatterforbundet says publishers now screen incoming manuscripts with AI detectors and authors are being rejected as 'written by AI' when they say they used none — it demands clear criteria before an algorithm gatekeeps literature.
items.rationale: A writers' union reports that publishers are rejecting manuscripts because an AI detector flagged them, and it demands criteria. This is a distinct event from the Horst analysis and from the earlier detector cards (NPR/Pangram, DOJ).

items.title: '죄와 벌' 속 한 문장‥AI는 '절했다', 번역가는?
items.excerpt: 도스토옙스키 작품 네 편을 번역하는 데 10년을 쓴 번역가가 '죄와 벌'의 한 문장을 두고 AI 번역과 사람 번역의 차이를 짚는다 — AI 문학 번역의 한계.
items.rationale: A fresh Korean broadcast feature: a translator compares one Crime and Punishment sentence as rendered by AI and by a human. It is a different piece and outlet from the 11-18 TCJ translation essay.

items.title: 'AI Slop' Papers Published Under Prominent Academics' Names
items.excerpt: High-profile researchers were listed as authors of AI-generated papers in little-known journals, raising concern Ph.D. students could be lured into submitting there too.
items.rationale: A new publishing-integrity incident: AI-generated papers carry real academics' names without their consent. This is a different event from the 11-23 card on hidden AI prompts found in journal papers.

items.title: Guest Post — Building a Taxonomy of Bots
items.excerpt: With AI crawlers and agents hammering scholarly platforms, a guest post proposes a shared taxonomy of bots so publishers can measure and manage robotic traffic.
items.rationale: Replacement pick: a concrete, usable framework from an on-list publishing outlet for classifying AI crawler and agent traffic. It moves on from the 11-07 CBC card, which reported the bot-swarm problem, to a proposed shared way of measuring and managing it.
